Private community messaging

Talk together, on your own server.

Trycord is group chat you can run yourself. Set up communities with their own channels, roles and permissions, talk one-to-one in direct messages, and let the server, not the browser, enforce who can do what. Point a domain at it and invite your group, or join an instance someone else runs.

  • Look around and try the demo without an account.
  • The same client in the browser and in a desktop app.
  • Permissions and moderation are enforced by the server, not the interface.

Why self-hosted

Software you run, for people you choose

Trycord is not a hosted service holding other people's conversations. It is a server you run, on a machine you control.

Your data stays on your instance

Messages, files and accounts live in your database. There is no upstream service they are mirrored to.

You decide who can join

Open registration, close it and invite by code, or run an instance only your community can reach. The server enforces it.

Migration is a setting, not a rebuild

Start on SQLite with no setup, move to MySQL when you grow, and keep your data. The choice is one environment variable.

What is in the box

The pieces a community actually uses

The parts a community leans on every day, from channels and roles to moderation and email.

Communities and channels

Every community has its own channels, members, roles and permissions, so conversation stays organised by topic.

Direct messages and friends

One-to-one conversations outside any community, with a friends list and presence so you can see who is around.

Moderation and appeals

Members report problems, moderators act, and a suspended account always has a path to appeal. Every action is recorded.

Accounts and email

Registration, email verification and password recovery, with SMTP for real deliveries.

Realtime by WebSocket

Messages, presence and typing arrive over one realtime gateway, with the REST API as the source of truth behind it.

Configured from the environment

Instance name, public URL, mail and database are environment variables, reviewed in one configuration screen in the app.

Find your people

Discover public communities

Communities that choose to be listed appear in the public directory. Search them, preview their channels, and open the one you want in the app. A community that is private does not appear anywhere.

Run it yourself

Start an instance in three steps

Install the server

Node with SQLite for a small instance, or Docker Compose with MySQL. A fresh install works with the defaults.

Point it at a domain

Set the public URL so links in email and invites are correct, and put a reverse proxy in front of it for TLS.

Invite who you want

Keep registration open, invite by code, or close the instance entirely. The server enforces whichever you choose.

Read the self-hosting guide

Your call

Join a community, or run the server yourself.

Open the app to join a community on an instance that already exists, or read the documentation and stand up your own. Either way it is the same software, and the server you are on is the one that holds your data.
